claims.text: In situ high-resolution TEM coupled with sequential EDS mapping can elucidate nanoprecipitate evolution and elemental redistribution during controlled oxidation.
Nanoprecipitates in Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 drive local elemental redistribution during oxidation.
Nanoprecipitate-driven elemental redistribution leads to more protective oxide scales.
The additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has a refined microstructure containing nanoscale precipitates.
Controlled in situ oxidation is proposed over approximately 800–1050 °C.
Nanoprecipitates undergo oxidation and act as focal points for elemental redistribution.
Selective oxidation of nanoprecipitates induces local elemental diffusion.
Preferential oxidation at precipitate interfaces redistributes alloying elements.
The redistribution of alloying elements promotes stable, protective oxide layers.
Protective oxide layers produced by this mechanism enhance oxidation resistance in the additively manufactured state.
In situ imaging will reveal morphological changes in nanoprecipitates during oxidation.
Sequential EDS maps will reveal local compositional shifts during oxidation.
Nanoprecipitate changes will correlate with dense, adherent oxide formation around the nanoprecipitates.
The additively manufactured alloy has better oxidation behavior than cast and wrought counterparts.
Cast and wrought variants of the same alloy have less pronounced nanoprecipitate refinement.
Cast and wrought variants consequently have lower oxidation resistance.
Spatial-resolution limits, electron-beam effects, and differences from industrial environments may constrain the interpretation of in situ TEM oxidation results.
Bulk thermogravimetric analysis can be used to compare oxidation kinetics with nanoscale in situ observations.
